translation: adj. 【课件】批评的；批判性的；挑剔的；极重要的；关键的；（病情）严重的，危急的
original_sentence: We also need to be critical about the information we receive and remember not to blindly trust what we have read.
definitionEn: expressing disapproval; extremely important or decisive; (of a situation) serious and dangerous.

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 极重要的；关键的（熟词生义，非「批评的」）
uncommonMeanings.example: Your decision is critical to our future.

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （病情、局势）严重的，可能有危险的
uncommonMeanings.example: One of the victims of the fire remains in a critical condition.
The review was critical of the film.

posExamples.sentence: The report was highly critical of the government. （课堂例句·这份报告对政府提出了强烈批评。）
Water is critical to the survival of all living things. （课堂例句·水对一切生物的生存都至关重要。）
The patient is in a critical condition. （课堂例句·这名病人情况危急。）

wordForms.noun: criticism (批评；批判) / critic (评论家；批评家)

idioms.example: The negotiations have reached a critical point.

collocations.translation: 有判断力的新闻读者（课件标题短语）
collocations.example: We should learn to be a critical news reader.

collocations.translation: 对……很挑剔（或提出批评）【课件】
collocations.example: Tom's parents were highly critical of the school.

collocations.translation: 对……起到关键的作用【课件】
collocations.example: Your decision is critical to our future.
Reducing carbon dioxide in the atmosphere is of critical importance.
Schools try hard to cultivate critical thinking.
Trust was a critical factor in their success.
One of the victims of the fire remains in a critical condition.
The article offers a critical analysis of the report.

synonyms.example: The next few weeks are crucial to the project.
synonyms.usage: 作表语或前置定语；表「至关重要」义时与 critical 互换，crucial 无「批评的」义。

synonyms.example: Clean water is essential to good health.
synonyms.usage: 作表语接 to sth / for sth；侧重「不可或缺」，不含「危急」义。

synonyms.example: Accurate figures are vital to the report.
synonyms.usage: 可作定语或表语，常接 to/for；强调不可缺少，不表示“批评的”。

advancedExpressions.expression: be critical of sb/sth / be critical to sth / critical point / of critical importance
advancedExpressions.example: Sleep is critical to health, and doctors are critical of our bad habits.

advancedExpressions.type: 构词法·-al 形容词后缀
advancedExpressions.expression: critic(n.评论家) + -al → critical(adj.批评的/关键的)；criticize(v.) / criticism(n.)
advancedExpressions.example: A critic writes criticism, so his articles are always critical.

advancedExpressions.expression: be critical to / be crucial to / be vital to / be essential to
advancedExpressions.example: Trust is critical to responsible journalism.

sentenceUpgrade.original: Your choice is very important to our future.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Your choice is critical to our future.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 用 be critical to 替换 very important to，更精炼有力。

sentenceUpgrade.original: Careful reading is very important.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Critical reading is essential.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 用 critical 突出“有分析判断力的”，并用 essential 提升表达。

classPractice.question: The journalists ____ ____ ____ (对……提出批评) the speaker's comments.
classPractice.note: 【课件语境应用】be critical of sb/sth 对……提出批评。

classPractice.question: Plans for the new factory have drawn fierce ____ (critical) from local people.
classPractice.note: 【课件语境应用】draw fierce criticism 招致猛烈批评，此处用名词。

classPractice.question: The new proposals have been ____ (critical) for not going far enough.
classPractice.note: 【课件语境应用】have been + 过去分词，被动语态，用动词 criticize。

classPractice.question: 你的决定对我们的未来至关重要。
classPractice.answer: Your decision is critical to our future.
classPractice.note: be critical to sth 起关键作用，介词用 to。

translation: vt. 【课件】使落入险境；使受困；用陷阱捕捉；n. 陷阱，夹子；圈套，诡计；困境，牢笼
original_sentence: The fire spread quickly through the tower block, leaving people on the upper floors trapped.
definitionEn: to catch or hold sb/sth so that they cannot escape or move; (n.) a device for catching animals, a trick, or a difficult situation.

uncommonMeanings.example: The clever question was a trap to make him confess.
He felt caught in the trap of an unhappy marriage.
The offer turned out to be a trap.

posExamples.sentence: When closing the car door, I trapped my coat in it. （课堂例句·关车门时，我的外衣被门夹住了。）
He found a deer with its leg in a trap. （课堂例句·他发现一头腿被夹在陷阱里的鹿。）
Smoke trapped the residents on the top floor. （课堂例句·浓烟把居民困在了顶层。）

wordForms.verb: trapped (被困的；被夹住的（作宾补/后置定语）) / trapping (使受困（现在分词/动名词）)
wordForms.adjective: trapped (被困的；被夹住的（作宾补/后置定语）)

idioms.idiom: fall into the trap of doing sth
idioms.meaning: 落入做某事的圈套；犯……的错误
idioms.example: Don't fall into the trap of believing every headline you read.

collocations.translation: 使某人被困（课文原句结构）
collocations.example: The fire left people on the upper floors trapped.
They were trapped in the cave and cried for help.
The police set traps to make the thief tell where the money was.

collocations.phrase: be caught in / fall into the trap of
collocations.translation: 落入……的圈套；陷入……的困境【课件】
collocations.example: Parents often fall into the trap of trying to do everything for their children.
After struggling for years, he finally escaped the poverty trap.
The false advert trapped him into paying in advance.
The animal managed to escape from the trap.
The ranger removed an illegal animal trap.

synonyms.example: The net was used to catch fish.
synonyms.usage: 及物动词，泛指抓住；trap 强调使其无法逃脱、陷入困境。

synonyms.example: The illness confined her to bed for a week.
synonyms.usage: 常用 be confined to；较正式，trap 更口语且含「陷阱/危险」意味。

advancedExpressions.expression: be trapped in / set a trap / fall into the trap of / the poverty trap
advancedExpressions.example: Once you fall into the trap of debt, you feel trapped in it for years.

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·V-ed 作宾语补足语
advancedExpressions.expression: leave + sb + done 让某人被…… → leaving people trapped 让人被困
advancedExpressions.example: The fire left people on the upper floors trapped; the storm left the road blocked.

advancedExpressions.expression: be trapped in / fall into a trap / set a trap / trap sb into doing
advancedExpressions.example: Do not let a false headline trap you into sharing it.

sentenceUpgrade.original: The fire made people on the upper floors unable to escape.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The fire left people on the upper floors trapped.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 用 leave sb trapped（leave + sb + 过去分词）替换 make ... unable to escape，更地道简洁。

sentenceUpgrade.original: The smoke made them unable to leave.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The smoke left them trapped upstairs.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 用 leave sb trapped 凝练表达“使某人受困”。

classPractice.question: The fire spread quickly, leaving many residents ____ (trap) on the upper floors.
classPractice.note: leave sb done 结构，人与 trap 是被动关系，用过去分词。

classPractice.question: The two miners ____ ____ (被困) underground for three days before being rescued.
classPractice.note: be trapped 被困，此处用一般过去时被动。

classPractice.question: 父母常常陷入事事替孩子代劳的误区。
classPractice.answer: Parents often fall into the trap of doing everything for their children.
classPractice.note: fall into the trap of doing sth 陷入做某事的误区。

classPractice.question: The police set a trick to catch the thief. → The police ____ ____ ____ to catch the thief.
classPractice.note: trap 作名词表「圈套」，set a trap 设圈套。

translation: vt. 【课件】公开，公布，发布；释放，放出；放开，松开；发泄，宣泄；n. 释放；泄露；（唱片/影片）发行，上映；解脱感
original_sentence: According to figures released by emergency services, dozens of people were injured in the fire.
definitionEn: to make sth available to the public; to set sb/sth free; to stop holding sth; to let out feelings.

uncommonMeanings.example: He refused to release her arm.
Exercise is a good way to release tension.
The new software is planned for release in April.
The album is ready for release.

posExamples.sentence: 10,000 balloons were released at the ceremony. （课堂例句·典礼上放飞了一万只气球。）
It has been 24 years since the release of the first Harry Potter book. （课堂例句·距第一本《哈利·波特》图书发布已过去24年。）
The agency released the figures at noon. （课堂例句·该机构在中午公布了数据。）

wordForms.noun: release (释放；发布；发行；解脱感)
wordForms.verb: released (被发布的；被释放的（作后置定语，如 figures released）)
wordForms.adjective: released (被发布的；被释放的（作后置定语，如 figures released）)

idioms.example: The film is now on general release across the country.

collocations.translation: 紧急服务部门公布的数字（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: According to figures released by emergency services, dozens were hurt.

collocations.phrase: release the latest news / a new album
collocations.translation: 发布最新消息／发行新专辑【课件】
collocations.example: The band will release a new album next month.

collocations.translation: 把某人从……释放；免除某人（义务）【课件】
collocations.example: The new law released employers from their obligation.

collocations.translation: 宣泄情绪／释放压力【课件】
collocations.example: She burst into tears, releasing all her negative emotions.
It's still seven weeks till the film's official release.
There was a sense of release after the exam.
Exercise can release tension after work.
The fire released toxic gases into the air.

synonyms.example: The results will be published next week.
synonyms.usage: 多指书刊、数据正式出版发表；release 更强调「向公众投放」，可用于消息、产品、影片。

synonyms.example: The government agreed to free the prisoners.
synonyms.usage: 作动词表「释放」时与 release 同义；release 更正式书面。

advancedExpressions.expression: release news 公布 / release sb 释放 / release one's arm 松开 / release tension 宣泄
advancedExpressions.example: The prison released him, and he released years of tension in tears.

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·V-ed 作后置定语
advancedExpressions.expression: figures released by emergency services = figures that were released ... 过去分词短语后置修饰名词，表被动
advancedExpressions.example: According to figures released by emergency services, dozens were injured.

advancedExpressions.expression: release sb from / release figures / release pressure / release sth into
advancedExpressions.example: The court released the man from custody.

sentenceUpgrade.original: According to the figures that were published by emergency services, ...
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: According to figures released by emergency services, ...
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 用过去分词短语 released by ... 替换定语从句 that were released by ...，更简洁。

sentenceUpgrade.original: The service published the figures.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The service released the latest figures.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 新闻语境中用 release figures 更地道。

classPractice.question: The bird ____ ____ (release) from the cage.
classPractice.note: 【课件语境应用】bird 与 release 是被动关系，用一般过去时被动。

classPractice.question: The firefighter took several hours to release the twins ____ the car in the water.
classPractice.note: 【课件语境应用】release sb from sth 把某人从……中救出。

classPractice.question: When is the best moment to release the date of the election ____ the newspapers?
classPractice.note: 【课件语境应用】release sth to sb 向……发布，介词用 to。

classPractice.question: 自第一本《哈利·波特》图书发布以来已经过去了24年。
classPractice.answer: It has been 24 years since the release of the first Harry Potter book.
classPractice.note: the release of sth 发布，此处 release 作名词。

translation: n. 救护车
original_sentence: Dozens of ambulances rushed to the scene to take the injured to hospital.
definitionEn: a vehicle with special equipment, used for taking sick or injured people to hospital.

uncommonMeanings.example: The hospital operates two air ambulances.

posExamples.sentence: An ambulance took the injured man to hospital. （课堂例句·一辆救护车把受伤的男子送往了医院。）
Someone called an ambulance immediately. （课堂例句·有人立即叫了救护车。）
He was taken to hospital by ambulance. （课堂例句·他由救护车送往医院。）

wordForms.noun: ambulances (救护车（复数）)

collocations.example: Quick, call an ambulance — he's badly hurt!

collocations.phrase: an ambulance arrives / rushes to the scene
collocations.example: Three ambulances rushed to the scene of the fire.
The injured were taken to hospital by ambulance.
The ambulance crew gave him first aid on the way.
The rural ambulance service needs more staff.
The ambulance crew treated him at the scene.
A new ambulance station opened nearby.
We heard an ambulance siren outside.

synonyms.example: Please give way to emergency vehicles.
synonyms.usage: 泛指救护车、消防车、警车等；ambulance 专指救护车。

advancedExpressions.expression: ambul-(行走) + -ance → ambulance「可移动的（医疗车）」；比较 distance / performance
advancedExpressions.example: The word ambulance once meant a mobile hospital that could move with the army.

advancedExpressions.expression: call an ambulance / dial the emergency number / send for help
advancedExpressions.example: In an emergency, call an ambulance immediately and stay calm.

advancedExpressions.expression: call an ambulance / reach the scene / give first aid / take sb to hospital
advancedExpressions.example: Call an ambulance and give first aid until it arrives.

sentenceUpgrade.original: A car for sick people came to take him to hospital.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: An ambulance rushed to take him to hospital.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 用专有名词 ambulance 替换啰嗦的 a car for sick people，并用 rush 增强急迫感。

sentenceUpgrade.original: They took him to hospital in an emergency vehicle.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: They took him to hospital by ambulance.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 用固定搭配 by ambulance 简洁表达交通方式。

classPractice.question: He was badly injured, so we quickly called an ____ to take him to hospital.
classPractice.note: call an ambulance 叫救护车，急救话题固定搭配。

classPractice.question: 伤者被救护车送往了最近的医院。
classPractice.answer: The injured were taken to the nearest hospital by ambulance.
classPractice.note: by ambulance 乘救护车，交通方式前不加冠词。

classPractice.question: Three ____ (ambulance) rushed to the scene of the accident.
classPractice.note: three 后接可数名词复数。

translation: vt. & vi. 【课件】使伸长，扩大，延期；扩大……的范围（涉及）；延伸，延续；[正式] 提供，给予（欢迎、邀请等）
original_sentence: By this time, the fire had extended to the 15th floor.
definitionEn: to make sth longer or larger; to reach or spread over an area; to offer or give sth such as a welcome or invitation.

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 延伸；延续（到某处/某时段）
uncommonMeanings.example: His writing career extended over a period of 40 years.

uncommonMeanings.meaning: [正式] 提供，给予（欢迎、款待、邀请）
uncommonMeanings.example: They extended hospitality to overseas students.

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 提供；给予（欢迎、帮助、邀请等）
uncommonMeanings.example: We extend our sympathy to the family.

posExamples.sentence: Follow these tips and you can extend your life. （课堂例句·遵循这些建议，你就可以延长寿命。）
Our land extends as far as the river. （课堂例句·我们的土地一直延伸到河边。）
The school extended the deadline by two days. （课堂例句·学校把截止日期延长了两天。）

wordForms.noun: extension (延长；伸展；延期；扩建部分)
wordForms.adjective: extensive (广阔的；大量的；广泛的) / extended (延长的（an extended holiday）；大的（an extended family 大家庭）)

collocations.translation: 已蔓延到15楼（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: By this time, the fire had extended to the 15th floor.

collocations.phrase: extend a road / a deadline / the range of products
collocations.translation: 扩建公路／延长期限／扩大产品范围【课件】
collocations.example: The school is extending the range of subjects taught.
The offer does not extend to employees' partners.

collocations.phrase: extend a warm welcome to sb
collocations.translation: 向某人表示热烈欢迎【课件·正式义】
collocations.example: I'm sure you will join me in extending a very warm welcome to our visitors.

collocations.translation: 向某人发出邀请【课件·正式义】
collocations.example: They extended an invitation to the professor.
The forest extends from the river to the hills.
The effects extend beyond the local area.
The investigation extended into a second week.

synonyms.example: The company plans to expand into Asian markets.
synonyms.usage: 侧重体积/规模向外扩张；extend 侧重长度/时间/范围的延伸。

synonyms.example: The treatment could prolong his life by a few years.
synonyms.usage: 只用于时间/持续时间的延长；extend 可用于时间、空间、范围。

advancedExpressions.expression: extend(v.) / extension(n.) / extensive(adj.) / extensively(adv.) / extended(adj.)
advancedExpressions.example: The extensive research took years, so they asked for an extension of the deadline.

advancedExpressions.expression: extend a deadline 延期 / extend to 涉及 / extend as far as 延伸到 / extend a welcome 给予欢迎
advancedExpressions.example: The road extends as far as the coast, and the tour now extends a warm welcome to families.

advancedExpressions.expression: extend to / extend from ... to ... / extend by / extend an invitation to
advancedExpressions.example: The road extends for ten kilometres.

sentenceUpgrade.original: By this time, the fire had spread to the 15th floor.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: By this time, the fire had extended to the 15th floor.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 课文用 extend 表「蔓延、扩大范围」，比 spread 更书面。

sentenceUpgrade.original: The damage reached another floor.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The damage extended to another floor before the fire was contained.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 用 damage extend to 表示受损范围扩大，并补出完整的过去时语境。

classPractice.question: 中国在世界事务中的影响力已大大扩大。
classPractice.answer: China has greatly extended its influence in world affairs.
classPractice.note: 【课件语境应用】extend one's influence 扩大影响力。

classPractice.question: 这个公园一直延伸到河边。
classPractice.answer: The park extends as far as the river.
classPractice.note: 【课件语境应用】extend as far as 延伸到，此处 extend 为不及物。

classPractice.question: 大家都玩得很开心，所以我们把聚会又延长了一个小时。
classPractice.answer: Everyone had a good time, so we extended the party for one more hour.
classPractice.note: 【课件语境应用】extend ... for one more hour 延长……一小时。

classPractice.question: The fire caused ____ (extend) damage to the whole tower block.
classPractice.note: 修饰名词 damage 用形容词 extensive「大量的、广泛的」。

translation: n. 【课件】建造，建设；建筑（物），结构；建筑业
original_sentence: There is concern that the construction company that built the tower block had not followed fire safety rules.
definitionEn: the process or industry of building sth; a structure or building; the way sth is built or put together.

uncommonMeanings.example: The tower is an impressive steel construction.
We studied the construction of the sentence.

posExamples.sentence: The station has been under construction for two years. （课堂例句·这座车站已经建了两年了。）
The bridge is still under construction. （课堂例句·这座桥仍在建设中。）
This sentence has an unusual construction. （课堂例句·这个句子的结构不同寻常。）

wordForms.noun: constructor (建造者；构造者)

collocations.translation: 建筑公司（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: The construction company had not followed fire safety rules.
The new bridge is still under construction.
Thousands of workers are employed in the construction industry.

collocations.translation: 一栋简单的木质建筑【课件】
collocations.example: They built a simple wooden construction by the lake.
The road is closed near the construction site.
Construction work will begin next month.
A construction worker reported the fault.
Construction costs have risen sharply.

synonyms.example: The building of the dam took ten years.
synonyms.usage: building 更口语常用；construction 更正式，且可指「建筑业、结构」。

synonyms.example: The bridge is a huge steel structure.
synonyms.usage: structure 强调「结构、构造」这一整体形态；construction 兼指「建造过程」与「建筑物」。

advancedExpressions.expression: construct(v.建造/确立) / construction(n.) / constructive(adj.建设性的) / constructor(n.)
advancedExpressions.example: They constructed the tower, but the construction ignored safety, so critics gave constructive advice.

advancedExpressions.expression: con-(共同) + struct(建立，词根「堆叠」) + -ion(名词) → construction；比较 structure / instruct / destruction
advancedExpressions.example: The root struct means 'to build', so construction, structure and instruct are all related.

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·同位语从句 + 定语从句连用
advancedExpressions.expression: There is concern that ... 中 that 引导同位语从句解释 concern；后一 that 引导定语从句修饰 the construction company
advancedExpressions.example: There is concern that the construction company that built the tower block had not followed fire safety rules.

advancedExpressions.expression: construct a building / construct an argument / under construction / constructive advice
advancedExpressions.example: She constructed a clear argument from reliable facts.

sentenceUpgrade.original: People worry that the company which built the block ignored safety rules.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: There is concern that the construction company that built the tower block had not followed fire safety rules.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 用 There is concern that ...（同位语从句）替换 people worry that ...，书面正式，并保留定语从句限定公司。

sentenceUpgrade.original: The company that built the tower ignored the rules.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The construction company failed to follow the safety rules.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 用 construction company 和 fail to do 提升正式度。

classPractice.question: The new stadium is still under ____ (construct) and will open next year.
classPractice.note: under construction 在建造中，介词后接名词。

classPractice.question: Instead of criticizing, she offered some ____ (construct) suggestions.
classPractice.note: 修饰 suggestions 用形容词 constructive「建设性的」。

classPractice.question: 有人担心这家建筑公司没有遵守消防安全规定。
classPractice.answer: There is concern that the construction company had not followed fire safety rules.
classPractice.note: There is concern that... 引导同位语从句，表「有人担心……」。

classPractice.question: They built a shelter with fallen branches. → They ____ a shelter out of fallen branches.
classPractice.note: construct sth out of/from sth 用……建造某物。

translation: n. 一打（十二个）；许多，大量（dozens of）
original_sentence: Dozens of people were injured in the fire, and several remained in a critical condition.
definitionEn: a group of twelve; (dozens of) very many.

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 许多，大量（dozens of，泛指很多，非确指12的倍数）

Keep the summary brief and factual. （课堂例句·摘要要简洁并以事实为依据。）

wordForms.noun: fact (事实)
wordForms.adverb: factually (如实地，就事实而言（other：fact + -ual「有……性质的」）)

collocations.translation: 事实性细节（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: The reports may contradict each other in terms of factual detail.
A good news reader checks whether the factual information is accurate.
The article gives a plain, factual account of what happened.
The editor found several factual errors in the draft.
Editors are responsible for factual accuracy.
Check whether each factual statement is supported.
The claim lacks factual evidence.
Factual reporting should avoid emotional language.

synonyms.example: The report must be accurate and free of mistakes.
synonyms.usage: accurate 强调「精确无误」；factual 强调「基于事实、非虚构」。二者常搭配 factual and accurate。

synonyms.example: A journalist should stay objective and not take sides.
synonyms.usage: objective 与 subjective 相对，强调「不带个人情感」；factual 侧重「以事实为依据」。

advancedExpressions.expression: 名词 + -ual 变形容词：fact→factual, habit→habitual, intellect→intellectual
advancedExpressions.example: A factual report sticks to facts, not to habitual assumptions.

advancedExpressions.expression: factual = fact-based = based on facts；辨真伪 tell fact from opinion
advancedExpressions.example: Readers should tell factual statements from opinions before believing a story.

advancedExpressions.expression: fact → factual → factually；反义表达 non-factual / inaccurate
advancedExpressions.example: The statement is factually inaccurate.

sentenceUpgrade.original: The two reports give different facts about the deaths.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The two reports differ in terms of factual detail about the deaths.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 用 differ in terms of factual detail 表达「在事实细节上有差别」，更贴合课文。

sentenceUpgrade.original: The report has mistakes about facts.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The report contains several factual errors.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 用 factual errors 是新闻审校的固定表达。

classPractice.question: The two news reports may contradict each other in terms of ____ (fact) detail.
classPractice.note: 名词修饰 detail 需用形容词 factual。

classPractice.question: A good reader should tell ____ (factual / emotional) statements from opinions.
classPractice.note: 语境为「区分事实与观点」，选 factual。

classPractice.question: 编辑在草稿中发现了几处事实性错误。
classPractice.answer: The editor found several factual errors in the draft.
classPractice.note: factual errors「事实性错误」。

translation: n. 例子，实例；情况，事例
original_sentence: For instance, the numbers of deaths differ from one report to another.
definitionEn: a particular example or case of something happening.

uncommonMeanings.example: There have been several instances of fires caused by old wiring.
In this instance, no correction was needed.

posExamples.sentence: This story is a good instance of how rumours spread online. （课堂例句·这个故事是谣言如何在网上传播的一个好例子。）
This is an instance of poor fact-checking. （课堂例句·这是事实核查不力的一个例子。）
In this instance, the later report was more accurate. （课堂例句·在这种情况下，后来的报道更准确。）

wordForms.noun: instance (例子，实例；情况) / instant (立即的；瞬间（other：形近词，勿混：instant「即刻」 vs instance「例子」）)
wordForms.adjective: instant (立即的；瞬间（other：形近词，勿混：instant「即刻」 vs instance「例子」）)

idioms.example: Many things can start a fire—a lit cigarette, for instance.
In the first instance, please report the problem to your manager.

collocations.translation: 例如，比如（课文原句词块，= for example）
collocations.example: For instance, the numbers of deaths differ from one report to another.
This is a clear instance of how facts can be reported differently.

collocations.translation: 在这种情况下，就此事而言
collocations.example: In this instance, both reports turned out to be inaccurate.
In the first instance, you should check the source of the news.
In many instances, the headline was misleading.
This was a rare instance of accurate prediction.
Consider each particular instance separately.
The inquiry began at the instance of local residents.

synonyms.example: Give me an example of what you mean.
synonyms.usage: for instance = for example，可互换；单独作名词时 example 更常用，an instance of 略正式。

synonyms.example: In some cases the reports were completely wrong.
synonyms.usage: case 侧重「具体情况、案例」；instance 侧重「作为例证的一件事」。in this instance ≈ in this case。

advancedExpressions.expression: for instance = for example = to give an example = take ... as an example
advancedExpressions.example: For instance, the death tolls differ; take the two reports as an example.

advancedExpressions.expression: for instance / an instance of / in this instance / in the first instance
advancedExpressions.example: In this instance, for instance, the numbers simply do not match.

advancedExpressions.expression: for instance / for example / such as / take ... as an example
advancedExpressions.example: Some details, for instance the time, may change.

sentenceUpgrade.original: For example, the numbers of deaths are not the same in the two reports.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: For instance, the numbers of deaths differ from one report to another.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 用 for instance 开头 + differ from one...to another 表「因报道而异」，更地道。

sentenceUpgrade.original: For example, the figures differ.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: For instance, the two reports give different figures.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 用完整举例句并明确比较对象。

classPractice.question: ____ ____, the numbers of deaths differ from one report to another.（例如）
classPractice.note: 课文原句；for instance = for example。

classPractice.question: This is a clear ____ (instance / instant) of how facts can be reported differently.
classPractice.note: 辨析形近词：instance「例子」，非 instant「瞬间」。

classPractice.question: 在这种情况下，两篇报道都不准确。（in this instance）
classPractice.answer: In this instance, both reports were inaccurate.
classPractice.note: in this instance「就此事而言，在这种情况下」。

translation: vi. 【课件】相异；有区别；不同于；（意见）相左，不同意
original_sentence: For instance, the numbers of deaths differ from one report to another.
definitionEn: to be different from sb/sth; to disagree with sb.

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 意见相左；不同意（differ with sb.）
uncommonMeanings.example: The young couple always differ over the education of their children.
Experts differ over the likely cause.

posExamples.sentence: People's tastes in films really differ. （课堂例句·人们对电影的品味确实不同。）
The two reports differ in tone. （课堂例句·这两篇报道在语气上不同。）
I differ with him on that point. （课堂例句·我在那一点上与他意见不同。）

wordForms.noun: difference (不同，差别)

collocations.example: The story Tom told the police differed from the one he told his mother.
The footprints in the desert differ in size and shape.

collocations.translation: 与某人在某事上有不同意见（课件归纳）
collocations.example: The two sides still differ with each other about the details of the plan.

collocations.translation: 对……有／没有／有一些影响（课件拓展）
collocations.example: Your age should make no difference to whether you get the job or not.
The two accounts differ widely.
The figures differ slightly from the estimate.
Opinions differ on the cause of the fire.
News habits differ from person to person.

synonyms.example: Prices vary from shop to shop.
synonyms.usage: vary 强调有变化幅度地不同，常接 from...to...；differ 常接 from sb/sth 表示与某物相异。

synonyms.example: I disagree with you on this point.
synonyms.usage: 作“意见相左”解时与 differ with sb 同义；disagree with sb about/on sth。

advancedExpressions.expression: differ from / differ in / differ with sb. about (on, over) sth.
advancedExpressions.example: Cultures differ from one another, and people differ in their values, but no one should differ with others over basic respect.

advancedExpressions.expression: differ from 与……不同；differ in 在……方面不同；differ with sb on sth 与某人意见不同
advancedExpressions.example: The reports differ from each other in tone.

advancedExpressions.expression: differ → difference → different → differently
advancedExpressions.example: Different journalists present the same event differently.

sentenceUpgrade.original: The two reports are not the same in the number of deaths.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The two reports differ in the number of deaths.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 用 differ in 替换 be not the same in，更简洁地道。

sentenceUpgrade.original: The reports are not the same.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The reports differ significantly in factual detail.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 用 differ in 精确指出差异维度。

classPractice.question: The story Tom told the police ____ from the one he told his mother. (differ)
classPractice.note: differ from 不同于；此处叙述过去，用过去式 differed。

classPractice.question: The footprints in the desert differ ____ size and shape.
classPractice.note: differ in 在……方面不同。

classPractice.question: The two sides still differ ____ the details of the plan.
classPractice.note: differ with sb. about/on/over sth.，句中省略 with each other，接方面用 about/over/on。

classPractice.question: 这对年轻的夫妇在孩子的教育上总是有分歧。
classPractice.answer: The young couple always differ over / on / about the education of their children.
classPractice.note: 两方直接作主语时用 differ over/on/about sth，无须再加 with each other。

classPractice.question: 你能否得到这份工作应该与你的年龄无关。
classPractice.answer: Your age should make no difference to whether you get the job or not.
classPractice.note: make no difference to 对……没有影响（differ 的名词拓展）。

translation: n. 【课件】结论；推论；结束，结局；（正式协议的）达成，签订
original_sentence: It would be wrong to rush to the conclusion that one of the news reports gives false information.
definitionEn: a judgement or decision reached by reasoning; the end or final part of sth; the formal and final arrangement of an official agreement.

uncommonMeanings.example: The two nations celebrated the successful conclusion of a trade treaty.
The story reached a happy conclusion.
The audience applauded at the conclusion of the speech.

posExamples.sentence: So what conclusion can we draw from this debate? （课堂例句·那么我们能从这场辩论中得出什么结论呢？）
Do not rush to a conclusion. （课堂例句·不要急于下结论。）
In conclusion, check more than one source. （课堂例句·总之，要核查不止一个消息来源。）

wordForms.noun: conclusion（目标词）

idioms.example: In conclusion, protecting the environment is everyone's duty.
It's unfair to jump to conclusions about someone you've just met.

collocations.phrase: come to / draw / reach / lead to a conclusion
collocations.example: After the debate we finally came to a clear conclusion.

collocations.translation: 所得结论是……（课件归纳，that 引导同位语从句）
collocations.example: The scientists came to the conclusion that the data were reliable.

collocations.translation: 贸然断定，过早下结论（课件归纳）
collocations.example: Don't rush to conclusions before you check the facts.
In conclusion, I'd like to thank everyone for their support.
The evidence supports a logical conclusion.
It is too early to reach a firm conclusion.
The data do not support that conclusion.
The headline led readers to a premature conclusion.

synonyms.example: You should use your own judgement rather than rely on rumours.
synonyms.usage: judgement 强调经过思考的判断力；conclusion 强调推理后所得的结论。

synonyms.example: The inference was based on limited evidence.
synonyms.usage: 可数名词；强调由证据推导的结果，conclusion 还可指事情的结束。

advancedExpressions.expression: conclude ... from ... / conclude ... with ... / It is concluded that ... / conclusive evidence
advancedExpressions.example: From the conclusive evidence, we can conclude that the report is false.

advancedExpressions.expression: draw/reach/come to a conclusion / jump to conclusions / in conclusion
advancedExpressions.example: We cannot draw a conclusion from one report.

advancedExpressions.expression: conclude → conclusion → conclusive；conclude from / conclude with
advancedExpressions.example: We concluded from the evidence that the report was false.

sentenceUpgrade.original: Finally, I want to thank my family.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: In conclusion, I'd like to express my thanks to my family.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 议论文结尾用 In conclusion 替换 Finally，更书面。

sentenceUpgrade.original: We decided that the claim was false.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: We drew the conclusion that the claim was false.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 用 draw the conclusion that 提升论证语体。

classPractice.question: So what can we ____ ____ ____ ____ (从这场辩论中得出结论)?
classPractice.note: conclude ... from ... 从……中得出结论（课件语境应用原题）。

classPractice.question: When the group discussion is nearing its end, make sure to ____ ____ ____ ____ ____ (以要点结束它).
classPractice.note: conclude ... with ... 以……结束（课件语境应用原题）。

classPractice.question: ____ ____ (最后), I'd like to express my thanks to my family.
classPractice.note: in conclusion 总之，最后（课件语境应用原题）。

classPractice.question: Only with solid facts ____ ____ ____ ____ ____ ____ (才能下结论).
classPractice.answer: can we come to a conclusion
classPractice.note: Only + 状语位于句首，主句部分倒装；come to a conclusion 下结论（课件语境应用原题）。

classPractice.question: The professor told us that research on the matter was far from ____ (conclude).
classPractice.note: far from + adj.，用形容词 conclusive 确凿的（课件语境应用原题）。

translation: adj. 【课件】错误的，不真实的；假的，人造的；虚伪的，不忠实的
original_sentence: It would be wrong to rush to the conclusion that one of the news reports gives false information.
definitionEn: not true or correct; not real but made to seem real; not sincere or loyal.

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 假的，人造的（不是天然的）
uncommonMeanings.example: The old lady wears false teeth.
He turned out to be a false friend.

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 人造的；假的（外观像真的）
uncommonMeanings.example: She wore false eyelashes.

posExamples.sentence: It is dangerous to draw a conclusion from false facts. （课堂例句·从虚假事实中得出结论是危险的。）
The report gave a false impression. （课堂例句·这篇报道给人造成了错误印象。）
The alarm was false. （课堂例句·这是一场假警报。）

wordForms.noun: falseness (虚假；不真实)

idioms.example: He got the money under false pretences.

collocations.translation: 虚假信息（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: We should be careful not to spread false information online.
Decide whether the following statements are true or false.
He checked in at the hotel under a false name.
The advertisement gives a false impression of the product.
The website repeated a false claim.
The fire alarm turned out to be a false alarm.
One source can create false confidence.
He obtained the document under false pretences.

synonyms.example: Your answer is wrong.
synonyms.usage: wrong 泛指错误；false 侧重“与事实不符、不真实”，也可指“假造的”。

synonyms.example: The painting turned out to be fake.
synonyms.usage: fake 强调蓄意伪造以欺骗；false 可中性指“非天然的（如 false teeth）”。

synonyms.example: The accusation is completely untrue.
synonyms.usage: 作定语或表语；语气直接，false 还可修饰身份、警报、印象等。

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·表示“虚假的”
advancedExpressions.expression: false / untrue / fake / misleading / inaccurate
advancedExpressions.example: A responsible reporter never spreads false, misleading or inaccurate information.

advancedExpressions.expression: false 指不真实或错误；wrong 指不正确；fake 指仿造品或故意伪造
advancedExpressions.example: The false claim used a fake image and the wrong date.

advancedExpressions.expression: false information / a false claim / misleading content / fabricated evidence
advancedExpressions.example: Fact-checkers exposed the fabricated evidence.

sentenceUpgrade.original: The news is not true.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The news turns out to be false and misleading.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 用 false and misleading 替换 not true，表达更精准有力。

sentenceUpgrade.original: The information was not true.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The report contained false and misleading information.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 用 false and misleading 准确区分不实与误导。

classPractice.question: The report gives ____ (false / wrong) information, which misleads many readers.
classPractice.note: 指信息“与事实不符、不真实”用 false。

classPractice.question: 我们不应该匆忙得出结论说这篇报道提供了虚假信息。
classPractice.answer: We should not rush to the conclusion that the report gives false information.
classPractice.note: rush to the conclusion that ... 匆忙断定；false information 虚假信息。

classPractice.question: The statement is not true. → The statement is ____.
classPractice.note: not true = false。

translation: n. 最小值，最少量，最低限度；adj. 最小的，最低的
original_sentence: To keep the report short, a journalist may reduce the number of casualties to the minimum.
definitionEn: the smallest amount or number that is possible or allowed; (adj.) smallest in amount or degree.

uncommonMeanings.example: There is a minimum charge of ten yuan for delivery.
Applicants must meet the minimum age requirement.

posExamples.sentence: Temperatures will fall to a minimum of five degrees tonight. （课堂例句·今晚气温将降至最低五度。）
The minimum age for driving is eighteen. （课堂例句·驾车的最低年龄是十八岁。）
Keep speculation to a minimum. （课堂例句·把猜测降到最低限度。）

wordForms.noun: minimum (最小值；最小的（复数 minima/minimums）)
wordForms.adjective: minimum (最小值；最小的（复数 minima/minimums）) / minimal (极小的，极少的)

collocations.example: The trip will take a minimum of three hours.
We should keep our costs to a minimum.
Safety rules help reduce the risk to a minimum.
Many part-time workers are paid the minimum wage.
At a minimum, check the date and source.
The article did the bare minimum of fact-checking.
The report meets the minimum requirements.
The minimum age is eighteen.

synonyms.example: That's the least I can do for you.
synonyms.usage: least 是 little 的最高级，可作限定词/代词；minimum 是名词，指“最低限度的量”。

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·“把……降到最低”
advancedExpressions.expression: keep/reduce sth to a minimum = minimize sth
advancedExpressions.example: To avoid mistakes, journalists should keep guesswork to a minimum and minimize bias.

advancedExpressions.expression: a minimum of 中 minimum 是名词；minimum standards 中作定语
advancedExpressions.example: A minimum of two sources is required.

advancedExpressions.expression: minimum 表规定或可能的最小值；minimal 表“极少的、微不足道的”
advancedExpressions.example: The task needs minimal effort but must meet minimum standards.

sentenceUpgrade.original: We should make the cost as small as possible.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: We should keep the cost to a minimum.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 用 keep ... to a minimum 替换 make ... as small as possible。

sentenceUpgrade.original: Use as little speculation as possible.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Keep speculation to a minimum.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 用 keep sth to a minimum 凝练表达“降至最低”。

classPractice.question: To save money, we should keep our spending ____ ____ ____ (最低限度).
classPractice.note: keep sth to a minimum 把……保持在最低限度。

classPractice.question: The whole project will take a ____ (minimum) of six months, and probably longer.
classPractice.note: a minimum of + 数量，用名词 minimum，意为“至少”；勿误用形容词 minimal。

classPractice.question: 严格的安全规定把事故的风险降到了最低。
classPractice.answer: The strict safety rules reduced the risk of accidents to a minimum.
classPractice.note: reduce sth to a minimum 把……减少到最低限度。

translation: n. 最大值，最大量，最高限度；adj. 最大的，最高的
original_sentence: Another journalist may raise the number of casualties to the maximum to attract more readers.
definitionEn: the greatest amount or number that is possible or allowed; (adj.) greatest in amount or degree.

uncommonMeanings.example: The maximum temperature today will be 35 degrees.
The maximum penalty is a heavy fine.

posExamples.sentence: The plane can reach a maximum of 900 kilometres an hour. （课堂例句·这架飞机时速最高可达900公里。）
The maximum load for this lift is 500 kilograms. （课堂例句·这部电梯的最大载重是500公斤。）
The hall holds a maximum of 300 people. （课堂例句·大厅最多容纳三百人。）

wordForms.noun: maximum (最大值；最大的（复数 maxima/maximums）)
wordForms.adjective: maximum (最大值；最大的（复数 maxima/maximums）) / maximal (最大的，最高的)

collocations.example: The lift can carry a maximum of eight people.
She used her time to the maximum during the exam.
The maximum speed on this road is 60 km per hour.
We should make the maximum use of natural light.
The service is operating at maximum capacity.
The form states the maximum amount allowed.
Check several sources for maximum benefit.
Place the warning first for maximum effect.

synonyms.example: This is the most I can offer you.
synonyms.usage: most 是 many/much 的最高级；maximum 是名词，指“允许或可能的最大量”，反义词为 minimum。

synonyms.example: Accuracy is our greatest concern.
synonyms.usage: great 的最高级，通常有 the 或物主限定词；maximum 常用于数值、容量和限度。

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·“最大限度地利用”
advancedExpressions.expression: make the maximum use of sth = maximize sth = make full use of sth
advancedExpressions.example: A wise reader maximizes the value of many sources and makes the maximum use of his own judgement.

advancedExpressions.expression: a maximum of 中作名词；maximum speed 中作定语
advancedExpressions.example: A maximum of nine deaths was estimated.

advancedExpressions.expression: maximum 指可达到或允许的最大值；maximal 较正式，指尽可能大的
advancedExpressions.example: The system operates at maximum capacity with maximal efficiency.

sentenceUpgrade.original: The bus can take 50 people at most.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The bus can take a maximum of 50 people.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 用 a maximum of 替换 at most，更书面正式。

sentenceUpgrade.original: Use this opportunity as fully as possible.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: We should make the most of this opportunity.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: make the most of 是“充分利用机会”的自然表达。

classPractice.question: This lift can carry ____ ____ ____ ____ eight people. (最多)
classPractice.note: a maximum of + 数量，意为“最多，至多”。

classPractice.question: The ____ (maximum / minimum) temperature today will be 35°C, the hottest this summer.
classPractice.note: 指“最高”气温用 maximum。

classPractice.question: 我们应该最大限度地利用这次机会。
classPractice.answer: We should make the most of this opportunity. / We should make maximum use of this opportunity.
classPractice.note: make the most of / make maximum use of 表示“充分利用”；不说 maximize this chance。

translation: n. 【课件】金额，款项；总和，总数；算术题；v. 总结，概括
original_sentence: As is reported, the athlete has been fined a large sum of money.
definitionEn: an amount of money; the total when numbers are added together; (verb) to give a summary of sth.

uncommonMeanings.example: The little boy is good at doing sums.
The teacher summed up the main points at the end of the lesson.
The sum of five and nine is fourteen.

posExamples.sentence: You'll be fined the sum of £200. （课堂例句·你将被处以200英镑的罚款。）
The charity received a large sum of money. （课堂例句·这家慈善机构收到了一大笔钱。）
Let me sum up the main points. （课堂例句·让我概括一下要点。）

wordForms.noun: summary (摘要，概要)

idioms.example: To sum up, we still have a lot of work to do.

collocations.example: He spent a large sum of money on the new car.
The sum of 4 and 5 is 9.
Can I just sum up what we've agreed so far?
In sum, the plan is both practical and creative.
The total sum was higher than expected.
The award was paid as a lump sum.

collocations.phrase: sum sth up in one word
collocations.example: Can you sum up the article in one word?

translation: 然而，不过，尽管如此（仍然）

collocations.translation: 分号连接前后转折的两个分句
collocations.example: The task was difficult; nevertheless, she finished it.
